--- STEM ---
Kestrelmoor Textiles Ltd runs a garment factory in Country X employing 150 machinists on day and night shifts. About 62 of the machinists are recent migrants whose first language is not English. Safety and quality instructions are issued as written English notices, and only 71% of migrant machinists passed last quarter's safety quiz, compared with 94% of other staff.

The factory manager must overcome this language barrier. Option one is to translate all safety and quality notices into 3 languages at a cost of $7,200. Option two is to pay 6 bilingual supervisors an extra $180 per month each to give verbal demonstrations on the line, costing $1,080 a month. Both options aim to cut the 9 safety incidents recorded last year.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'communication barrier'.
    Answer: A communication barrier is anything that stops a message being received or understood correctly, such as language differences, noise, jargon, poor timing or unclear wording. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Anything that blocks or distorts a message between sender and receiver; Examples include language, noise, jargon and unclear wording

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two barriers to communication at Kestrelmoor Textiles.
    Answer: Barrier 1: Language differences [k], 62 of the 150 machinists are recent migrants whose first language is not English, so written English notices are not fully understood [app]. Barrier 2: Over-reliance on written English notices [k], only 71% of migrant machinists passed last quarter's safety quiz compared with 94% of other staff [app].
    Keywords: 150 machinists, written English notices, 71%, 94%, language barrier, safety quiz, 3 languages
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Language difference blocks understanding of messages; Using an unsuitable method (written-only) blocks understanding | application_max_2: 62 of the 150 machinists are recent migrants whose first language is not English; Only 71% of migrant machinists passed the safety quiz versus 94% of other staff

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of option one, translating the notices into 3 languages.
    Answer: Advantage 1: All migrant machinists receive instructions in their own language [k], so the 62 recent migrants would understand written safety and quality notices without depending on a supervisor being present [app], reducing the gap between the 71% and 94% pass rates [an]. Advantage 2: Translation is a one-off cost with no ongoing fees [k], at $7,200 once compared with $1,080 every month for bilingual supervisors [app], saving money after about 7 months and keeping instructions available at all times [an].
    Keywords: $7,200, $1,080, 3 languages, recent migrants, 71%, 94%, safety and quality notices
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Instructions in the reader's own language remove the language barrier; A one-off translation has no recurring monthly cost | application_max_2: 62 recent migrants would understand notices without a supervisor present; $7,200 once versus $1,080 a month for bilingual supervisors | analysis_max_2: Pass rates should rise towards the 94% benchmark of other staff; Translation is cheaper after about 7 months and always available

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think the factory manager should translate the notices instead of paying bilingual supervisors? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for translating the notices is the one-off cost of $7,200 [k], which would give all 62 recent migrants written instructions in 3 languages, cheaper than $1,080 a month for supervisors after about 7 months [app], reducing the language barrier that left only 71% passing the safety quiz [an]. However, one argument against is that written notices cannot demonstrate tasks [k], so machinists who struggle to read in any language would still fail, while verbal demonstrations by 6 bilingual supervisors would show safe machine operation directly on the line [app], which better suits practical garment work and immediate questions [an]. Overall, the manager should choose option two, the bilingual supervisors [eval], because hands-on demonstration overcomes the language barrier more reliably in a factory, and it can be scaled back once pass rates reach 94% and the 9 safety incidents fall [eval].
    Keywords: $7,200, $1,080 a month, 3 languages, recent migrants, 71%, 94%, bilingual supervisors
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Translated written instructions remove the language barrier permanently; Verbal demonstration teaches practical tasks and allows questions | application_max_2: $7,200 once for 3 languages versus $1,080 a month for 6 bilingual supervisors; Only 71% of migrant machinists passed the safety quiz versus 94% of others | analysis_max_2: Permanent translated notices close the comprehension gap at low cost; Written-only methods cannot teach physical machine operation | evaluation_max_2: Weighs both the translation and the bilingual supervisor options; Reaches a justified recommendation using stem figures

--- STEM ---
Brackmore Insurance Services runs a customer call centre in Country X with 88 call-handlers answering about 30,000 calls a month. Call quality is monitored by a small team of 4 quality coaches. Complaints are logged by handlers, and a weekly email tells all staff the top 5 complaint types. Handlers receive no individual feedback and never hear what happened to complaints they logged.

Only 12% of staff in last year's survey felt their feedback was acted on. The centre manager proposes monthly one-to-one feedback meetings between team leaders and handlers, using about 140 staff-hours a month. Team leaders instead suggest a daily 10-minute briefing with the whole team, which would take no extra time beyond shift handovers. Waiting times already average 9 minutes, so staff motivation matters.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'feedback'.
    Answer: Feedback is the response sent back to the sender of a message, showing whether it was received and understood, or giving a reaction to a performance, idea or action. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Response returned to the sender of a message; Shows whether the message was understood or comments on performance

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two reasons why feedback is important for Brackmore call-handlers.
    Answer: Reason 1: Feedback tells handlers whether their work meets standard [k], so the 88 call-handlers would know how they performed on the about 30,000 calls a month [app]. Reason 2: Feedback motivates employees and helps them improve [k], which matters because only 12% of staff felt their feedback was acted on last year [app].
    Keywords: 88 call-handlers, 30,000 calls, 12%, weekly email, top 5, one-to-one, 10-minute briefing
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Feedback tells employees whether their work meets the standard; Feedback motivates employees and supports improvement | application_max_2: 88 call-handlers answer about 30,000 calls a month; Only 12% of staff felt their feedback was acted on last year

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two problems of relying only on the weekly email of complaint types.
    Answer: Problem 1: The email is one-way and gives no personal comment [k], so the 88 handlers cannot learn how their own handling of the about 30,000 calls a month could improve [app], limiting learning and call quality [an]. Problem 2: Emails list only the top 5 complaint types [k], so unusual or individual issues raised by handlers are never acknowledged, consistent with only 12% feeling their feedback was acted on [app], leaving staff feeling ignored and demotivated [an].
    Keywords: weekly email, top 5, 88, 30,000, 12%, one-to-one feedback meetings, 140 staff-hours
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: One-way channels give no personal, tailored guidance; Summaries hide individual and unusual issues | application_max_2: 88 handlers answer 30,000 calls a month with no individual feedback; The weekly email lists only the top 5 complaint types and 12% felt heard | analysis_max_2: Without tailored guidance, call quality and learning stagnate; Ignored handlers become demotivated and waiting times may rise

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think the centre manager should introduce monthly one-to-one feedback meetings instead of daily team briefings? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for one-to-one meetings is that handlers receive personal feedback [k], using about 140 staff-hours a month to discuss individual performance, which would address the finding that only 12% of staff felt their feedback was acted on [app], so handlers would know exactly how to improve their handling of the about 30,000 calls a month [an]. However, one argument against is the time cost [k], as 140 staff-hours a month is the equivalent of about 18 working days, and a daily 10-minute briefing with the whole team would cost no extra time beyond shift handovers [app], reaching all 88 handlers daily instead of once a month [an]. Overall, the centre should combine both, starting with the daily briefings and adding monthly one-to-one meetings for struggling handlers [eval], because briefings cost nothing extra while one-to-ones fix the deeper motivation problem behind the 12% figure [eval].
    Keywords: 140 staff-hours, 12%, 10-minute briefing, 88, 30,000, one-to-one, weekly email
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: One-to-one feedback is personal but time-consuming; Group briefings are broad, cheap and can be frequent | application_max_2: 140 staff-hours a month is about 18 working days of one-to-one time; Only 12% of staff felt their feedback was acted on last year | analysis_max_2: Personal feedback addresses individual performance on 30,000 calls; Daily briefings cost nothing extra and reach everyone far more often | evaluation_max_2: Weighs both the one-to-one meetings and daily briefings; Reaches a justified recommendation using stem figures

--- STEM ---
Ruskin & Cole Department Store in Country X employs 210 people across 2 selling floors and a warehouse. The store turns over $24 million in sales a year. Head office communicates every change, till updates, floor moves and rota rules, by email and memo, and full staff meetings are held only twice a year. A staff survey found 58% of employees did not understand the last 3 changes, and staff turnover rose to 34% this year.

Regional manager Dana Cole proposes fortnightly 45-minute team briefings where staff can ask questions; the finance director prefers a quarterly newsletter costing $300 per edition, about $1,200 a year. Dana argues face-to-face questions would catch confusion early, but the finance director notes the briefings would use about 158 staff-hours each fortnight across all 210 employees. The newsletter would reach all 210 employees.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'two-way communication'.
    Answer: Two-way communication is communication where the receiver can respond to the sender, such as a conversation, meeting or phone call, allowing questions and feedback. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Message flows in both directions with feedback; Allows questions and clarification, unlike one-way channels

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two benefits of two-way communication at the store.
    Answer: Benefit 1: Staff can ask questions and clear up confusion immediately [k], so the 58% of employees who did not understand the last 3 changes could be brought up to date in fortnightly briefings [app]. Benefit 2: Managers learn what employees think [k], helping the store reduce the staff turnover that rose to 34% this year by showing staff their views matter [app].
    Keywords: 58%, last 3 changes, turnover, 34%, 210, twice a year, fortnightly
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Two-way channels allow questions and immediate clarification; Two-way channels make staff feel heard and valued | application_max_2: 58% of employees did not understand the last 3 changes; Staff turnover rose to 34% this year

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two problems caused by one-way email and memo communication at Ruskin & Cole.
    Answer: Problem 1: One-way messages cannot be questioned [k], so the 58% of staff who misunderstood recent till updates and rota rules had no chance to ask about them between staff meetings held only twice a year [app], causing mistakes and frustration on the shop floor [an]. Problem 2: One-way communication makes staff feel unheard [k], which may explain why staff turnover rose to 34% this year, with employees leaving rather than raising concerns by email to head office [app], increasing recruitment and training costs [an].
    Keywords: email and memo, twice a year, 58%, 34%, head office, 45-minute team briefings, quarterly newsletter
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: One-way messages cannot be questioned or clarified; One-way communication leaves staff feeling ignored | application_max_2: 58% of staff misunderstood recent changes, meetings held only twice a year; Staff turnover rose to 34% this year amid email and memo communication | analysis_max_2: Unquestioned instructions cause mistakes and frustration on the shop floor; Feeling unheard drives staff turnover and raises recruitment costs

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Ruskin & Cole should introduce fortnightly team briefings instead of a quarterly newsletter? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for the briefings is that they are two-way [k], letting the 210 staff ask questions about till updates and rota rules, attacking the 58% misunderstanding directly, at a cost of about 158 staff-hours each fortnight [app], which should reduce errors, the 34% staff turnover and disruption to the $24 million sales [an]. However, one argument against is cost and reach [k], as 158 staff-hours every fortnight is far more expensive in time than a $300 quarterly newsletter costing about $1,200 a year, which reaches everyone in print [app], but the newsletter is one-way and would not fix the misunderstanding driving the 34% turnover [an]. Overall, the store should introduce the fortnightly team briefings [eval], because two-way face-to-face communication addresses the root cause, and falling turnover would save far more than the briefings cost [eval].
    Keywords: 45-minute team briefings, $300, $1,200, twice a year, 58%, 34%, 210
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Two-way face-to-face briefings check understanding; A printed newsletter is cheap and reaches everyone but is one-way | application_max_2: 158 staff-hours each fortnight to answer the 58% misunderstanding; $300 per edition, about $1,200 a year for the newsletter | analysis_max_2: Two-way dialogue reduces errors, turnover of 34% and disruption to $24 million sales; The one-way newsletter would not fix the misunderstanding causing turnover | evaluation_max_2: Weighs both the fortnightly briefings and the quarterly newsletter; Reaches a justified recommendation using stem figures

Castlereagh Solicitors is a law firm in Country X with 52 staff across 3 offices. The partners plan to merge with a rival firm, Trelawney & Grant, moving 30 staff into new premises 12 miles away and creating 12 new roles. No announcement has been made; rumours have spread through the grapevine and 7 staff have resigned in 2 months.

The managing partner must decide how to announce the merger. Option one is an all-staff meeting followed by written letters to every employee. Option two is to issue a press release this week first; the partners believe it would reassure clients of continuity, but staff would hear of the merger from the media.     Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Communication via the official, authorised channels of the organisation; Examples include official letters, meetings, memos and press releases

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of formal communication for Castlereagh Solicitors.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Formal channels carry authority and accuracy [k], so an all-staff meeting followed by letters would tell all 52 staff the official merger details rather than grapevine rumours [app]. Advantage 2: Formal written records can be referred back to [k], so the 30 staff moving to premises 12 miles away would have clear written terms about their relocation and the 12 new roles [app].
    Keywords: 52 staff, all-staff meeting, grapevine, 30 staff, 12 miles, 12 new roles, written letters
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Official channels are accurate and carry authority; Written formal records can be referred back to | application_max_2: All 52 staff would hear official details instead of rumours; 30 staff moving 12 miles away would have written terms on the 12 new roles

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two problems caused by rumours and informal communication about the merger.
    Answer: Problem 1: Rumours are inaccurate and uncontrolled [k], so staff imagine job losses across the 3 offices even though the plan creates 12 new roles and relocates 30 staff rather than cutting jobs [app], fuelling anxiety and resignations [an]. Problem 2: Informal communication undermines trust in management [k], which is why 7 staff resigned in 2 months without any official announcement being made [app], risking client service and jeopardising the $2.4 million deal [an].
    Keywords: grapevine, 7 staff, 2 months, 12 new roles, $2.4 million, 3 offices, Trelawney & Grant
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Rumours are inaccurate and cannot be controlled by the business; Silence from management damages trust and morale | application_max_2: Rumours ignore the 12 new roles and 30 staff relocation across 3 offices; 7 staff resigned in 2 months before any official announcement | analysis_max_2: Imagined job losses fuel anxiety and resignations; Resignations risk client service and the $2.4 million deal

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Castlereagh should tell staff first through an all-staff meeting and letters rather than issuing a press release this week? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for telling staff first is that it is honest and builds trust [k], so the 52 staff would hear directly from the managing partner before a press release, preventing more resignations like the 7 staff who left in 2 months [app], protecting morale and client service during the $2.4 million merger [an]. However, one argument against is that a press release this week would reassure clients and protect the firm's reputation sooner [k], because rival firms may already know about the merger talks [app], yet staff hearing first from the media would feel betrayed and may leave before the 12 new roles are filled [an]. Overall, the firm should hold the all-staff meeting and written letters first, then issue the press release [eval], because committed staff are essential during a merger and a one-week delay for clients is a small price compared with losing key lawyers [eval].
    Keywords: all-staff meeting, press release, 52 staff, 7 staff, $2.4 million, 12 new roles, written letters
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Telling staff first builds trust and commitment; Early public announcement reassures clients and protects reputation | application_max_2: 52 staff would hear directly, stopping the 7 resignations seen in 2 months; Press release first would reach clients sooner but staff would feel betrayed | analysis_max_2: Honesty protects morale, client service and the $2.4 million deal; Media-first news risks losing staff before the 12 new roles are filled | evaluation_max_2: Weighs both announcing to staff first and issuing a press release first; Reaches a justified recommendation using stem figures

Wrenhill Toys Ltd sells the wooden 'Sunshine Express' train set through 160 retailers across Country X; about 9,000 units were sold last year. The train set sells for $45 and is the firm's best-selling toy this Christmas. A small number of units contain loose magnets, a choking risk identified by the safety regulator, and 340 sets have already been returned by parents.

The marketing manager proposes an urgent press release and social media campaign to alert buyers quickly. The managing director prefers phoning all 160 retailers and writing to the 2,100 buyers who registered online, costing about $6,500 and taking 2 weeks; only retailers and the media can reach the remaining 6,900 unregistered buyers.   Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'written communication'.
    Answer: Written communication is the passing of information through written words, such as letters, emails, memos, reports, notices or text messages, producing a record that can be read and re-read. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Communication using written words; Examples include letters, emails, reports and notices; creates a record

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of written communication for the product recall.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Written messages give a permanent record [k], so the 160 retailers would have the recall instructions in writing to identify and return the unsafe Sunshine Express sets [app]. Advantage 2: Written communication suits messages sent to named individuals [k], so the 2,100 buyers who registered online would receive clear return instructions by letter [app].
    Keywords: 160 retailers, 2,100, 9,000, 340, $6,500, 2 weeks
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Written messages create a permanent, checkable record; Written messages suit sending the same message to named individuals | application_max_2: 160 retailers would have recall instructions in writing for the unsafe sets; 2,100 registered online buyers would receive return instructions by letter

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of announcing the recall through a press release and social media.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Mass electronic channels reach far more people far faster [k], alerting the 6,900 unregistered buyers who never registered online [app], so unsafe Sunshine Express sets can be returned before more magnets are swallowed [an]. Advantage 2: Posting online costs almost nothing [k], compared with about $6,500 and 2 weeks for phone calls and letters to retailers and registered buyers [app], protecting public safety and the brand at minimal cost [an].
    Keywords: press release, social media, 6,900 unregistered, 9,000, $6,500, 2 weeks, 160 retailers
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Mass media and social media reach huge audiences quickly; Electronic public announcements cost very little | application_max_2: 6,900 unregistered buyers would be reached instantly; Compared with about $6,500 and 2 weeks for phone calls and letters | analysis_max_2: Faster alerts return unsafe sets before more injuries occur; Minimal cost protects both public safety and the brand's reputation

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Wrenhill Toys should rely on the press release and social media instead of phoning retailers and writing to registered buyers? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for the press release and social media is speed and reach [k], which would instantly alert the owners of the remaining 6,900 unregistered units, including the 340 sets already proving defective [app], so children could be protected immediately at almost no cost [an]. However, one argument against is that mass media cannot guarantee every affected buyer acts [k], whereas phoning the 160 retailers and writing to the 2,100 registered buyers uses two-way and written channels with confirmed receipt, costing about $6,500 and 2 weeks [app], giving an auditable recall record for the safety regulator [an]. Overall, Wrenhill should use both: the press release immediately to protect children, followed by calls and letters to retailers and registered buyers to evidence the recall [eval], prioritising safety over the $6,500 cost [eval].
    Keywords: press release, social media, 160 retailers, 2,100, $6,500, 6,900, 340
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Mass media is fast and wide-reaching but unverifiable; Two-way and written channels confirm receipt and create records | application_max_2: Press coverage reaches the 6,900 unregistered buyers instantly; Phoning 160 retailers and writing to 2,100 registered buyers costs about $6,500 | analysis_max_2: Immediate public alert prevents further injuries from loose magnets; Confirmed calls and letters give an auditable record for the regulator | evaluation_max_2: Weighs both the public campaign and direct two-way contact; Reaches a justified recommendation using stem figures

--- STEM ---
Hartham Bakery is a family-run private limited company founded in 2003 in the market town of Bramfield. It employs 24 bakers, shop assistants and delivery drivers, producing artisan loaves and cakes for 3 retail outlets across Country X, and generated $520,000 in annual sales revenue last year. The owner, Priya Raman, plans to replace the retiring production supervisor who has managed the bakery floor for 9 years.

Priya has a recruitment budget of $4,500 and wants the new supervisor in post within 8 weeks. Two internal candidates, both senior bakers with 6 and 4 years at the bakery, have expressed interest, while an experienced supervisor from a rival bakery has also applied after Priya placed a small advert in the local newspaper. Priya must decide whether to promote internally or appoint the external candidate.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'job description'.
    Answer: A document that sets out the main tasks, duties and responsibilities of a particular job, and usually the hours, pay and reporting relationships. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Lists the tasks, duties and responsibilities of a job; May include hours, pay and reporting relationships

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two reasons why Hartham Bakery should carry out a job analysis before recruiting the new production supervisor.
    Answer: Reason 1: Job analysis identifies exactly what the job involves [k], for example the daily tasks of managing the bakery floor, stock control and 24 staff across 3 retail outlets [app]. Reason 2: Job analysis ensures the advert and selection criteria match the role [k], so Priya attracts suitable candidates within the $4,500 recruitment budget rather than wasting money on unsuitable applicants [app].
    Keywords: Hartham Bakery, production supervisor, $4,500, 8 weeks, Priya, 3 retail outlets, bakery floor
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Job analysis identifies tasks and requirements of the job; Job analysis ensures the advert and criteria match the role | application_max_2: Managing the bakery floor and 24 staff across 3 retail outlets; $4,500 budget and need for suitable applicants

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two benefits to Hartham Bakery of producing a clear job description for the supervisor vacancy.
    Answer: Benefit 1: A job description tells candidates exactly what the job involves [k], so applicants for the production supervisor role understand the bakery-floor duties before applying [app], reducing unsuitable applications and saving Priya time and the $4,500 budget [an]. Benefit 2: A job description gives the interviewer a checklist for comparing candidates [k], allowing internal and external applicants to be scored against the same duties [app], making the final choice more objective and lowering the risk of a poor appointment [an].
    Keywords: Hartham Bakery, production supervisor, $4,500, Priya, bakery floor, internal candidates, 8 weeks
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Tells candidates exactly what the job involves; Provides a checklist for comparing candidates fairly | application_max_2: Production supervisor applicants understand bakery-floor duties; Internal and external applicants scored against the same list | analysis_max_2: Fewer unsuitable applications saves time and budget; Objective scoring reduces the risk of a poor appointment

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Hartham Bakery should appoint the production supervisor from outside the business rather than promote internally? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for appointing externally is that the rival-bakery supervisor brings fresh ideas and proven experience [k], and has already applied after Priya placed the advert in the local newspaper [app], which could raise standards on the bakery floor and protect the $520,000 sales revenue [an]. However, appointing externally overlooks the 2 internal candidates with 6 and 4 years at the bakery [k], who already know the 24 staff, the 3 retail outlets and Priya's plans [app], so promotion could boost morale and loyalty across the workforce [an]. Overall, Hartham Bakery should promote internally if one candidate clearly matches the job description and person specification [eval], because the lower cost, faster replacement within 8 weeks and stronger motivation outweigh the extra ideas an external hire might bring [eval].
    Keywords: Hartham Bakery, $4,500, 8 weeks, Priya, 24, rival bakery, $520,000
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: External hire brings fresh ideas and experience; Internal promotion boosts morale and uses known staff | application_max_2: Rival-bakery supervisor applied via the newspaper advert; Two internal candidates with 6 and 4 years at the bakery | analysis_max_2: Fresh ideas could raise standards and protect $520,000 revenue; Promotion aids motivation, loyalty and continuity within 8 weeks | evaluation_max_2: Weighs external fresh ideas against internal loyalty and cost; Reaches a justified judgement conditional on candidate fit

    Question: Define the term 'person specification'.
    Answer: A document that states the qualifications, skills, experience and personal qualities a person needs to do a particular job. [2].

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two requirements that should be included in the person specification for the graduate civil engineer posts.

Requirement 2: Practical technical skills [k], such as reading drawings and operating measurement equipment needed on the 14 bridge inspection and refurbishment contracts [app].
    Keywords: Norwick, 1998, 58, $1.6 million, person specification, $2,800, Tomasz
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Academic qualifications relevant to the job; Practical technical skills or experience for the job | application_max_2: Only 1 of 3 internal applicants holds a degree; Reading drawings and operating measurement equipment on 14 contracts

  Qc [6 marks]

Benefit 2: It links appointees to the real demands of the job [k], so graduates appointed to the inspection team can handle technical drawings, measurement equipment and safety reports [app], reducing costly mistakes across 14 active bridge contracts [an].

    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Provides objective criteria for comparing candidates; Links the selected candidate to the job's demands | application_max_2: All 40 external applicants and 3 internal crew scored consistently; Graduates able to handle drawings, measurement equipment and reports | analysis_max_2: Consistent scoring makes selection fairer and defensible; Competent appointees reduce mistakes on 14 bridge contracts

  Qd [8 marks]

Overall, Norwick should appoint externally for these graduate posts [eval], because the inspection team needs degree-level expertise that the internal pool largely lacks, and the $2,800 advert cost is justified by safer, more reliable bridge work [eval].
    Keywords: Norwick, person specification, $2,800, $1.6 million, Tomasz, technical drawings, 58 engineers
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: External recruitment widens the pool and brings new skills; Internal promotion rewards loyalty and uses known staff | application_max_2: 40 external applicants, many degree holders, $2,800 adverts; Only 1 of 3 internal applicants holds a degree | analysis_max_2: Degree-level expertise supports safe bridge inspection work; Promoting unqualified staff could raise error risk on contracts | evaluation_max_2: Weighs external expertise against internal loyalty and morale; Reaches a justified judgement favouring external appointments

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two reasons why the content of Wellbridge Pharmacies' job advertisement is important.
    Answer: Reason 1: Clear advert content attracts the right applicants [k], so stating the 5 branches need qualified pharmacists for 2 retirements will deter unqualified candidates from applying [app]. Reason 2: The advert shapes how applicants view the employer [k], which matters because pharmacists choose employers carefully and 1,100 weekly customers expect professional service [app].
    Keywords: Wellbridge Pharmacies, $6,000, 2 pharmacists, 1,100 customers, Dr. Ellen Marsh, 5 community pharmacies
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Advert content attracts suitable and deters unsuitable applicants; The advert shapes how applicants view the employer | application_max_2: Qualified pharmacists needed for 2 retirements in June; 1,100 weekly customers expect professional service

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of using a free online job site for the pharmacist vacancies rather than the national press.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Using an online site saves money [k], preserving the $6,000 budget instead of spending $2,400 on each national press advert [app], so Wellbridge keeps recruitment costs low while filling 2 vacancies [an]. Advantage 2: Online adverts can be placed and reach candidates quickly [k], which is vital with the 2 pharmacists retiring in June [app], reducing the risk of reduced opening hours or temporary branch closures [an].
    Keywords: Wellbridge Pharmacies, $6,000, $2,400, June, 2 pharmacists, online job site
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Online advertising saves money compared with press adverts; Online adverts can be placed and seen quickly | application_max_2: $6,000 budget saved instead of $2,400 per press advert; 2 pharmacists retiring in June creates urgency | analysis_max_2: Lower costs leave money for training or retention; Fast filling avoids reduced hours or branch closures

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Wellbridge Pharmacies should advertise the pharmacist vacancies in the national pharmacy press rather than on free online job sites? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for the national press is wider reach among qualified pharmacists [k], since 2 press adverts costing $4,800 would be seen by candidates across the country, not just near the 5 branches [app], raising the chances of filling both June vacancies with genuinely qualified staff [an]. However, the press route absorbs most of the $6,000 budget [k], while the free online site cost nothing last year although it produced only 5 weak applications [app], so relying on online alone risks failing to hire and forcing the branches to reduce services for 1,100 weekly customers [an].     Keywords: Wellbridge Pharmacies, $6,000, $2,400, June, 5 weak applications, 1,100 customers, online job site
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: National press reaches a wider pool of qualified candidates; Online advertising is free but may attract fewer suitable candidates | application_max_2: 2 press adverts costing $4,800 reach candidates nationwide; Online site produced only 5 weak applications last year | analysis_max_2: Wider reach raises the chance of filling both June vacancies; Relying on online risks reduced services for 1,100 weekly customers | evaluation_max_2: Weighs advertising cost against reach and urgency; Reaches a justified judgement favouring the national press

    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Studying a job to identify tasks and responsibilities; Identifying skills and working conditions involved

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two reasons why the Corvane Grand Hotel should carry out a job analysis before advertising the chef vacancies.

Reason 2: It produces accurate adverts and selection criteria [k], so candidates know the work involved before the $240,000 July wedding bookings begin [app].
    Keywords: Corvane Grand Hotel, $1.9 million, 74 staff, $3,000, 6 weeks, Sandra Iwu, job analysis
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Job analysis identifies tasks and conditions of the jobs; Job analysis produces accurate adverts and criteria | application_max_2: Head chef and commis chef roles in a 110-room 4-star kitchen; $240,000 of July wedding bookings the chefs must support

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two problems that could arise if the hotel advertised the chef posts without a job analysis.

Problem 2: The chosen chefs may be wrong for the kitchen [k], arriving to find a pace and menu unsuited to them despite the 6-week timescale [app], leading to early resignation and renewed short-staffing of the 19 kitchen staff [an].

    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Adverts may misdescribe the jobs without job analysis; Appointees may be unsuited to the role without analysis | application_max_2: Unsuitable applicants before the $240,000 July weddings; Chefs arriving to find an unsuited pace, renewing staff shortages | analysis_max_2: Wasted time and budget on failed selection; Early resignation recreates short-staffing among 19 kitchen staff

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think the Corvane Grand Hotel should complete the job analysis before advertising rather than advertise the chef posts immediately? Justify your answer.

    Keywords: Corvane Grand Hotel, $1.9 million, $240,000, $3,000, 6 weeks, Sandra Iwu, job analysis
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Immediate advertising saves time during urgent vacancies; Job analysis improves match between candidate and job | application_max_2: 3 weeks' notice and $1.9 million revenue at risk in peak season; $3,000 budget and 6-week target need efficient selection | analysis_max_2: Rushing risks jeopardised July weddings and guest satisfaction; Careful analysis makes the 6-week process more likely to succeed | evaluation_max_2: Weighs speed against selection quality; Reaches a justified judgement favouring prior job analysis

--- STEM ---
Brackmoor Haulage Ltd is a private limited company operating a distribution depot in the industrial city of Varenne, Country X. Founded in 2005, it employs 63 drivers, pickers and depot staff, running 28 lorries on contract delivery routes, and last year handled 42,000 pallets worth $2.3 million in revenue. The managing director, Elena Petrova, must recruit a replacement urgently. She could promote Dani Whitmore, the shift supervisor with 7 years at the depot, who knows all 28 routes and the 42,000-pallet contract intimately. Dani earns $34,000 now; the manager role pays $48,000.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'internal recruitment'.
    Answer: Filling a job vacancy by appointing or promoting someone who already works for the business. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Appointing or promoting from the existing workforce; Filling a vacancy without hiring from outside

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages to Brackmoor Haulage Ltd of recruiting the operations manager internally.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Internal candidates know the business [k], so Dani Whitmore already understands the 28 routes and the 42,000-pallet contract [app]. Advantage 2: Internal recruitment is fast and cheap [k], costing little and taking 2 weeks instead of spending $5,500 and waiting for external applications [app].
    Keywords: Brackmoor Haulage Ltd, $5,500, Dani Whitmore, 28 lorries, 2 weeks, $2.3 million, Elena Petrova
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Internal candidates already know the business and its operations; Internal recruitment is faster and cheaper than external hiring | application_max_2: Dani knows the 28 routes and the 42,000-pallet contract; Promotion costs little and takes 2 weeks instead of $5,500

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two disadvantages to Brackmoor Haulage Ltd of promoting Dani Whitmore to operations manager.
    Answer: Disadvantage 1: Internal promotion leaves skills gaps elsewhere [k], so promoting Dani from shift supervisor creates a new vacancy among the 63 drivers and depot staff [app], requiring further recruitment and training [an]. Disadvantage 2: Dani has no experience managing a depot budget [k], despite the manager role paying $48,000 compared with her current $34,000 [app], so errors with budgets and contracts could threaten the $2.3 million revenue if she is not trained quickly [an].
    Keywords: Brackmoor Haulage Ltd, $48,000, $34,000, Dani Whitmore, $2.3 million, 63 drivers, depot budget
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Promotion creates a vacancy elsewhere in the business; Internal candidates may lack experience for the higher role | application_max_2: Dani's promotion leaves a supervisor gap among 63 staff; Dani has never managed a depot budget, role pays $48,000 | analysis_max_2: Further recruitment and training needed, adding cost and time; Budget inexperience could threaten $2.3 million revenue if unsupported

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Brackmoor Haulage Ltd should promote Dani Whitmore rather than recruit an external operations manager? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for promoting Dani is continuity and speed [k], since she knows the 28 routes and the 42,000-pallet contract and can start within 2 weeks at no advertising cost [app], keeping deliveries for key customers on track and protecting $2.3 million revenue in a crisis caused by the sudden March resignation [an]. However, Dani has never managed a depot budget [k], and external managers might bring fresh ideas and proven financial control that could justify the $5,500 advertising cost [app], so promoting her without support risks costly budgeting mistakes across the whole depot operation [an]. Overall, Brackmoor should promote Dani, but only with structured support such as budget training and mentoring from Elena Petrova [eval], because her route knowledge and 7 years' experience outweigh her inexperience, provided the business invests in her development [eval].
    Keywords: Brackmoor Haulage Ltd, Dani Whitmore, $5,500, 2 weeks, $2.3 million, 28 lorries, Elena Petrova
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Internal promotion offers speed, low cost and continuity; External hires may bring proven budgeting skills and fresh ideas | application_max_2: Dani knows routes and the contract, starts in 2 weeks at no cost; Dani has never managed a budget; external route costs $5,500 | analysis_max_2: Continuity protects $2.3 million revenue after a sudden resignation; Without support, budget inexperience could cause costly mistakes | evaluation_max_2: Weighs internal continuity against external budgeting expertise; Reaches a justified judgement favouring promotion with structured support

--- STEM ---
Hallowell Insurance Group is a public limited company running a call centre in the city of Mercester, Country X. Founded in 1995, it employs 240 call handlers and team leaders answering about 18,000 calls a month for car and home insurance policies. To support a major expansion, the group needs to recruit 12 new call handlers by September.

The HR manager, Jonas Lindqvist, has shortlisted 30 candidates from 190 applications received in May. He plans to interview each shortlisted candidate for 20 minutes before 2 managers, at a cost of about $60 in manager time per interview, making roughly $1,800 in total. Alternatively, he could add a practical telephone-simulation assessment day costing $2,400, where candidates handle scripted calls scored by supervisors.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'selection'.
    Answer: The process of choosing, from all applicants, the candidate who best fits the job and the business, using methods such as shortlisting, interviews and tests. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Choosing from all applicants the best candidate; Using methods such as shortlisting, interviews and tests

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two reasons why interviews are a useful selection method for the 12 call handler posts.
    Answer: Reason 1: Interviews let managers assess communication skills face to face [k], which matters when handlers will answer about 18,000 calls a month for car and home policies [app]. Reason 2: Interviews let candidates and the group judge fit [k], so candidates can ask about the 240-strong team and the September deadline [app].
    Keywords: Hallowell Insurance Group, $1,800, 190 applications, 30 candidates, 12 new call handlers, 18,000 calls, Jonas Lindqvist
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Interviews assess communication skills directly; Interviews help both sides judge fit for the job | application_max_2: Handlers must answer 18,000 calls a month on insurance policies; Candidates can ask about the 240-strong team and September deadline

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two limitations of relying on interviews alone to select the call handlers.
    Answer: Limitation 1: Interviews measure confidence more than competence [k], so a polished candidate may impress for 20 minutes yet struggle with real customer calls after September [app], raising the risk of poor performance and early resignation [an]. Limitation 2: Interviews are costly in management time [k], at $60 per candidate across 30 interviews costing roughly $1,800, yet still cannot reveal telephone skills [app], so the group may misjudge hires and face expensive repeat recruitment [an].
    Keywords: Hallowell Insurance Group, $1,800, $2,400, 30 candidates, 20 minutes, 18,000 calls, Jonas Lindqvist
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Interviews measure confidence rather than competence; Interviews consume significant management time | application_max_2: A polished 20-minute performance may not reflect call-handling reality; $60 per interview, roughly $1,800 total, without revealing phone skills | analysis_max_2: Poor hires raise underperformance and turnover after September; Repeat recruitment would add further cost to the group

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Hallowell Insurance Group should add the $2,400 telephone-simulation assessment day rather than rely on interviews alone? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for the assessment day is that it tests real job performance [k], with candidates handling scripted calls scored by supervisors rather than talking about themselves for 20 minutes [app], giving far better evidence of who can manage 18,000 calls a month on live policies [an]. However, the assessment day adds $2,400 to the roughly $1,800 interview cost, taking the total to around $4,200 [k], and for a mass-hiring of 12 handlers the extra detail may not be worth the added spend in manager time [app], especially when September is close and interviews alone are standard practice [an]. Overall, Hallowell should add the telephone-simulation day for the 12 posts [eval], because call handling is the core of the job and the extra $2,400 is far cheaper than training the wrong 12 people [eval].
    Keywords: Hallowell Insurance Group, $2,400, $1,800, 30 candidates, 18,000 calls, Jonas Lindqvist, 12 new call handlers
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Assessment centres and simulations test real job performance; Interviews are cheaper and adequate for mass hiring | application_max_2: $2,400 simulation tests scripted calls scored by supervisors; Total cost near $4,200 against 12 urgent September hires | analysis_max_2: Simulation evidence better predicts handling 18,000 live calls; Extra cost may not pay back for 12 similar posts | evaluation_max_2: Weighs simulation cost against selection accuracy; Reaches a justified judgement favouring the assessment day

====================================================================================================

--- STEM ---
Ashgrove Care Home is a privately owned residential care home founded in 2010 in Country X, with 64 residents supported by 85 care staff and 12 kitchen and maintenance workers. Last year it filled 9 care vacancies and received over 500 applications. The manager, Deborah Clarke, found many free-style CVs arrived in different lengths and layouts, making fair comparison of candidates very difficult for the shortlisting panel.

Deborah is redesigning the process so every applicant completes a standard application form covering qualifications, care experience, references and a short statement about why they want to care for elderly people. Forms cost about $2 per applicant to print and process, and the home spent $1,000 on recruitment advertising last year. Two senior carers prefer CVs, arguing they show personality and achievements better than forms.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'curriculum vitae'.
    Answer: A document prepared by a job applicant summarising their personal details, education, qualifications, experience and skills. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Document prepared by the applicant; Summarises details, qualifications, experience and skills

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages for Ashgrove Care Home of using a standard application form instead of free-style CVs.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Standard forms make comparison easy [k], so the shortlisting panel can score the 500-plus applicants against the same care experience and references [app]. Advantage 2: Forms ensure key information is never missing [k], such as why each applicant wants to care for the 64 residents [app].
    Keywords: Ashgrove Care Home, $1,000, $2 per applicant, 64 residents, Deborah Clarke, 9 care vacancies, application form
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Standard forms make candidates easy to compare; Forms guarantee all key information is provided | application_max_2: Shortlisting panel comparing 500+ applicants consistently; Statement of why they want to care for 64 residents always included

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two limitations of using application forms alone for the care vacancies.
    Answer: Limitation 1: Forms restrict what candidates reveal [k], so the personality and achievements that two senior carers value may never reach the panel [app], meaning the home could miss warm, suited carers for the 64 residents [an]. Limitation 2: Forms take effort to complete [k], which may deter the very 9 scarce care applicants the home needs right now [app], slowing the refilling of vacancies and adding pressure on the 85 existing care staff [an].
    Keywords: Ashgrove Care Home, 64 residents, 85 care staff, 9 care vacancies, Deborah Clarke, $2 per applicant, application form
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Forms restrict what candidates can show about themselves; Forms can deter some candidates from applying | application_max_2: Personality and achievements that senior carers value may be hidden; Completion effort may deter the 9 care applicants needed | analysis_max_2: Risk of missing warm, suited carers for residents; Fewer applicants adds pressure on the 85 existing care staff

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Ashgrove Care Home should require all applicants to complete the standard application form rather than accept CVs? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for mandatory forms is fair, consistent comparison [k], because the panel can score every one of the 500-plus applications against the same qualifications, references and statements about caring for the 64 residents [app], reducing bias and making the shortlist defensible [an]. However, forms add roughly $2 per applicant to process and may put off strong candidates who prefer CVs [k], which the two senior carers argue show personality and achievements far better [app], risking a smaller, blander applicant pool for the 9 urgent care vacancies [an]. Overall, Ashgrove should require the standard application form [eval], because fairness and completeness matter most when comparing hundreds of applicants, while a brief CV may still be attached voluntarily [eval].
    Keywords: Ashgrove Care Home, $2 per applicant, 64 residents, 500 applications, 85 care staff, Deborah Clarke, 9 care vacancies
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Forms allow fair, consistent comparison of many applicants; Forms add cost and may deter CV-preferring candidates | application_max_2: 500+ applications scored against identical criteria for 64 residents; $2 per applicant cost; senior carers prefer CV insight into personality | analysis_max_2: Consistent scoring reduces bias and strengthens the shortlist; Deterred candidates could shrink the pool for 9 urgent vacancies | evaluation_max_2: Weighs consistency and fairness against candidate-friendliness; Reaches a justified judgement favouring mandatory form completion

SET ID: P1_U2_SET_159
UNIT: Unit 2: People in Business
====================================================================================================

--- STEM ---
Ferrybrook Distribution Ltd is a private limited company running a regional e-commerce fulfilment warehouse in Country X. Founded in 2019, it employs 96 warehouse operatives and forklift drivers, picking about 26,000 orders a month. With the Christmas peak approaching, it needs to recruit 20 temporary warehouse operatives within 6 weeks. Order volumes are expected to rise by 40% in December and January.

The operations director, Marcus Boateng, is choosing between two selection methods for the 60 shortlisted candidates. He could hold 15-minute interviews with each candidate, costing about $900 in supervisor time, or ask all 60 to sit a 45-minute numeracy and spatial-awareness aptitude test costing $14 per candidate, $840 in total. Last year, 35% of interview-based hires left within 3 months.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'aptitude test'.
    Answer: A test that measures a candidate's natural ability or potential to learn and perform tasks, such as numeracy, literacy or spatial awareness. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Measures natural ability or potential to learn; Covers abilities such as numeracy or spatial awareness

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two ways the aptitude test could help Ferrybrook Distribution Ltd select the 20 temporary operatives.
    Answer: Way 1: The test objectively measures job-relevant ability [k], checking whether candidates can handle numeracy and spatial tasks needed to pick 26,000 orders a month [app]. Way 2: The test is fast and uniform across all 60 shortlisted candidates [k], making results easy to compare within the 6-week hiring deadline [app].
    Keywords: Ferrybrook Distribution Ltd, $840, $900, 60 shortlisted candidates, 6 weeks, 26,000 orders, Marcus Boateng
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: The test measures job-relevant abilities objectively; The test is uniform and quick to score across candidates | application_max_2: Numeracy and spatial skills needed for 26,000 monthly orders; 60 candidates compared consistently within the 6-week deadline

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two limitations of using aptitude tests alone for the warehouse roles.
    Answer: Limitation 1: Tests measure ability, not attitude [k], so a high-scoring candidate might still skip shifts during the Christmas peak [app], raising turnover above last year's 35% for interview-based hires and triggering re-training costs [an]. Limitation 2: Tests cannot judge teamwork or reliability [k], yet temporary operatives must work safely alongside 96 staff moving fast-moving orders [app], so poor hires may cause injuries or errors that disrupt the 26,000-order monthly flow [an].
    Keywords: Ferrybrook Distribution Ltd, 35%, 60 shortlisted candidates, 26,000 orders, 96 warehouse operatives, Marcus Boateng, aptitude test
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Tests measure ability rather than attitude or reliability; Tests cannot judge teamwork or safety behaviour | application_max_2: High scorers may not sustain attendance in the Christmas peak; Temporary staff working alongside 96 staff on fast orders | analysis_max_2: Higher turnover adds re-training and overtime costs beyond 35%; Poor teamwork or unsafe behaviour disrupts the 26,000-order flow

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Ferrybrook Distribution Ltd should use the $840 aptitude test rather than the $900 interviews for the temporary operatives? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for the aptitude test is accuracy at scale [k], scoring all 60 shortlisted candidates on job-relevant numeracy and spatial skills for $840, less than the $900 interview cost [app], which should reduce mis-hires and the 35% early turnover Ferrybrook suffered last year [an]. However, interviews reveal attitude, motivation and safety awareness [k], which the Christmas peak demands more than raw test scores [app], so replacing interviews entirely could repeat last year's 35% turnover if attitude-blind hires are made [an]. Overall, Ferrybrook should use the $840 test as the first stage and keep short 15-minute interviews for the best scorers [eval], combining objective ability data with a check on attitude within the 6-week deadline [eval].
    Keywords: Ferrybrook Distribution Ltd, $840, $900, 60 shortlisted candidates, 35%, 6 weeks, aptitude test
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Aptitude tests measure job-relevant ability objectively and cheaply; Interviews reveal attitude, motivation and safety awareness | application_max_2: $840 test scores all 60 candidates on numeracy and spatial skills; Last year 35% of interview-based hires left within 3 months | analysis_max_2: Objective scores should reduce mis-hires and early turnover; Attitude-blind hiring risks repeating the 35% turnover rate | evaluation_max_2: Weighs test efficiency against interview insight; Reaches a justified judgement favouring a combined two-stage approach

--- STEM ---
Greenhollow Supermarkets Ltd is opening its 4th supermarket in Country X next spring. Founded in 2014, the group employs 310 staff across 3 existing stores and generated $9.5 million in sales last year. The new 12,000 square foot store needs 48 new employees, including a store manager, 6 supervisors and 41 shop assistants, all starting before the May opening date.

The group HR director, Katherine Doyle, proposes a 1-day assessment centre for the 6 supervisor roles, with group exercises, role-plays and a written test, costing $3,600. Alternatively, she could run one-to-one interviews with all 96 shortlisted candidates, costing $1,500 in management time. She wants the strongest 6 supervisors in post early so they can then help train the 41 shop assistants before opening week.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define the term 'assessment centre'.
    Answer: A selection method in which several candidates take part in a range of exercises, such as group tasks, role-plays and written tests, assessed by trained observers. [2].
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Several candidates take part in varied exercises; Trained observers assess group tasks, role-plays and written tests

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of using an assessment centre to select the 6 supervisors.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Assessment centres observe real behaviour [k], revealing how each of the 96 shortlisted candidates handles group exercises and role-plays like actual supervisor dilemmas [app]. Advantage 2: Several assessors can score each candidate [k], reducing personal bias when choosing just 6 supervisors from 96 candidates [app].
    Keywords: Greenhollow Supermarkets Ltd, $3,600, $1,500, 6 supervisors, 96 shortlisted candidates, Katherine Doyle, $9.5 million
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Observes candidates' actual behaviour in realistic tasks; Multiple assessors reduce individual bias | application_max_2: 96 candidates observed on group exercises and role-plays; Just 6 supervisors chosen, so bias reduction matters

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two drawbacks of using an assessment centre for the supervisor roles.
    Answer: Drawback 1: Assessment centres are expensive to run [k], costing $3,600 against $1,500 for one-to-one interviews with all 96 candidates [app], an extra $2,100 that strains the pre-opening budget of a new 12,000 square foot store [an]. Drawback 2: Assessment centres need time and staff to organise [k], with a full day of role-plays and written tests before May [app], risking delay if the store manager and 6 supervisors are still not in post for training the 41 shop assistants [an].
    Keywords: Greenhollow Supermarkets Ltd, $3,600, $1,500, 96 shortlisted candidates, 41 shop assistants, Katherine Doyle, 12,000 square foot
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Assessment centres are expensive compared with interviews; Assessment centres require significant organisation and time | application_max_2: $3,600 versus $1,500 interviews, an extra $2,100; Needs a full day before May opening and 41 shop assistants to train | analysis_max_2: Extra $2,100 strains the new store's pre-opening budget; Delay risks leaving supervisors unable to train 41 assistants

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Greenhollow Supermarkets Ltd should use the $3,600 assessment centre rather than interviews costing $1,500 for the 6 supervisor posts? Justify your answer.
    Answer: One argument for the assessment centre is selection quality [k], as group exercises and role-plays reveal how 96 candidates cope with supervisor-type conflicts and team leadership [app], giving the best chance of appointing 6 supervisors strong enough to train 41 shop assistants before May [an]. However, the assessment centre costs $3,600, $2,100 more than interviews [k], and for a cost-conscious 4-store group generating $9.5 million, that difference could fund part of the 41 assistants' training [app], making interviews the leaner option if supervisor ability is already evident [an]. Overall, Greenhollow should use the $3,600 assessment centre [eval], because the 6 supervisors will shape the new store's culture and staff performance, so the selection accuracy is worth the extra $2,100 [eval].
    Keywords: Greenhollow Supermarkets Ltd, $3,600, $1,500, 96 shortlisted candidates, 41 shop assistants, 6 supervisors, $9.5 million
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Assessment centres select more accurately through observed exercises; Interviews are cheaper and may reveal obvious ability | application_max_2: 96 candidates observed on group exercises and role-plays; $3,600 centre versus $1,500 interviews, a $2,100 difference | analysis_max_2: Better selection underpins training 41 shop assistants before May; The $2,100 saving is modest against $9.5 million group sales | evaluation_max_2: Weighs selection accuracy against the extra $2,100 cost; Reaches a justified judgement favouring the assessment centre

--- STEM ---
Tarnmere Retail Group operates 6 supermarket stores across Country X and employs 240 staff. The group is opening a new store in Bramfield next spring and must hire 30 sales assistants before March. Last year, the HR team received 1,400 CVs for just 25 vacancies, and managers found that one-third of applicants omitted key details such as previous retail experience or weekend availability.

The HR manager wants to introduce a standard application form for the Bramfield campaign, arguing that every candidate would answer the same questions and shortlisting would be faster and fairer. The store general manager prefers keeping CVs, believing they reveal personality and written communication skills that a form cannot capture. Designing and printing the new form will cost $600, and two managers would spend about 2 days each on the changeover.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define 'application form'.
    Answer: An application form is a document containing a standard set of questions that all applicants for a vacancy must complete. It asks for personal details, qualifications and employment history so the employer can compare candidates on equal terms. [2]
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Document containing standard/set questions completed by all applicants; Requests personal details, qualifications and employment history for comparison

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two benefits to Tarnmere Retail Group of using an application form for the Bramfield campaign.
    Answer: Benefit 1: Application forms contain standard questions, so every one of the 1,400 applicants answers the same way [k], making shortlisting for the 30 sales assistant posts in Bramfield faster and fairer for managers [app]. Benefit 2: Forms force every candidate to provide key details such as retail experience, which one-third of last year's CVs omitted [k], so the HR team avoids wasting time on incomplete applications for the Bramfield campaign [app]. [4]
    Keywords: application form, 1,400, 30 sales assistants, Bramfield, retail experience, one-third
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Standard questions mean all candidates answer identically; Ensures key information is supplied by every applicant | application_max_2: Shortlisting 1,400 applicants for 30 Bramfield posts becomes faster and fairer; Solves the problem that one-third of last year's CVs omitted key details such as retail experience

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of using CVs for selecting sales assistants.
    Answer: Advantage 1: A CV lets each applicant present their skills and experience in their own way [k], revealing personality and written communication skills [app], so managers can judge how well a candidate would represent Tarnmere Retail Group in busy stores [an]. Advantage 2: CVs are quick and inexpensive for applicants to create and send [k], helping the group attract a large pool such as the 1,400 candidates it received last year [app], which increases the chance of finding excellent sales assistants for Bramfield [an]. [6]
    Keywords: CV, CVs, personality, written communication skills, 1,400, Bramfield, sales assistants
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: CV allows applicants to present skills and experience in their own format; CVs are quick and cheap for applicants to produce and send | application_max_2: Reveals personality and written communication skills the store general manager values; Helped attract 1,400 candidates when 25 vacancies were filled last year | analysis_max_2: Better judgement of fit for customer-facing supermarket stores; Wider applicant pool raises the likelihood of appointing strong sales assistants for Bramfield

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Tarnmere Retail Group should introduce the application form for the Bramfield campaign? Justify your answer.
    Answer: Tarnmere Retail Group should introduce the application form because the 1,400 applicants would all answer identical questions [k], allowing two managers to shortlist the 30 sales assistants quickly and fairly, with about 2 days each on design a small one-off effort for the group [app]. This would also solve the problem of one-third of CVs omitting key details such as retail experience [an]. However, the store general manager prefers CVs because they reveal personality and written communication skills [k], which matter when staff speak to shoppers all day in 6 supermarket stores [app], and losing that insight could mean appointing assistants who perform poorly with customers and need replacing [an]. Overall, on balance the group should adopt the application form for the Bramfield campaign because consistency and speed at a scale of 1,400 applicants outweigh the extra insight CVs give for entry-level sales roles, with communication skills still checked at interview [eval]. The $600 cost is trivial compared with the wages and disruption of a poor appointment across 6 supermarket stores [eval].
    Keywords: application form, 1,400, 30 sales assistants, Bramfield, one-third, $600, written communication skills, 6 supermarket stores
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Application forms standardise answers across all candidates; CVs reveal personality and written communication skills | application_max_2: Consistent shortlisting of 1,400 applicants for 30 Bramfield posts by two managers; Removes the one-third of CVs that omitted key details such as retail experience | analysis_max_2: Fairer, faster shortlisting and fewer wasted management hours; Risk that strong interpersonal candidates are filtered out before interview | evaluation_max_2: Balanced judgement that consistency wins at 1,400-applicant scale; Acknowledges $600 cost and the role of interview in checking communication skills

--- STEM ---
Voss Engineering Ltd manufactures hydraulic pumps for agricultural machinery and employs 85 production staff at its plant in Dunwick. The company needs to hire 6 graduate production engineers to support four automated production lines, and has shortlisted 18 candidates from 320 applications received this year. The HR director believes practical aptitude tests would show which candidates can read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems before interviews are held.

The production manager argues that aptitude tests cost $1,800 to administer and take half a day to run, whereas one-to-one interviews cost almost nothing and reveal motivation and teamwork. The managing director must decide whether to test the 18 candidates or simply interview them and appoint the 6 best-performing interviewees within three weeks.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define 'aptitude test'.
    Answer: An aptitude test is a selection method that measures a candidate's natural ability to carry out specific tasks, such as numerical reasoning or reading technical drawings. Employers use the results to predict how well a candidate can learn and perform the duties of the job. [2]
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Selection method measuring natural ability for specific tasks; Used to predict how well a candidate can learn and perform the job

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two benefits of using aptitude tests for the graduate engineer recruitment.
    Answer: Benefit 1: Aptitude tests give objective, measurable scores, so all 18 shortlisted candidates are assessed against the same practical tasks [k], helping the HR director identify which candidates can read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems for the 6 graduate engineer roles [app]. Benefit 2: Testing before interviewing filters out unsuitable candidates early [k], so the company avoids wasting interview time and fills the 6 posts within three weeks [app]. [4]
    Keywords: aptitude tests, 18 candidates, engineering drawings, 320 applications, $1,800, Dunwick
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Objective and measurable scores for every candidate; Filters out unsuitable candidates before interview | application_max_2: Checks ability to read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems; Supports appointing 6 graduate engineers within three weeks

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of one-to-one interviews as a selection method for Voss Engineering Ltd.
    Answer: Advantage 1: One-to-one interviews let the panel explore each candidate's motivation and teamwork [k], revealing qualities that the $1,800 aptitude tests cannot measure [app], so the production manager can judge whether a graduate fits the working culture at the Dunwick plant [an]. Advantage 2: Interviews are inexpensive to set up and run [k], which matters when filling 6 posts from a shortlist of 18 candidates [app], helping Voss Engineering Ltd control recruitment costs while assessing every candidate properly [an]. [6]
    Keywords: one-to-one interviews, motivation and teamwork, Dunwick, 85 production staff, $1,800, 6 graduate production engineers
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Explores motivation and teamwork in depth; Inexpensive to set up and run | application_max_2: Reveals qualities tests cannot measure, such as motivation and teamwork; Low cost suited to filling 6 posts from 18 candidates | analysis_max_2: Better judgement of cultural fit at the Dunwick plant; Controls recruitment costs for a small engineering firm

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Voss Engineering Ltd should use aptitude tests before interviewing the 18 candidates? Justify your answer.
    Answer: Voss Engineering Ltd should use aptitude tests because they produce objective scores for all 18 candidates [k], allowing the HR director to check who can actually read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems rather than relying on interview impressions alone [app]. With 320 applications and only 6 graduate engineer roles, an evidence-based shortlist reduces the risk of a costly mis-hire in a technical manufacturing environment [an]. However, the production manager argues that one-to-one interviews cost almost nothing and reveal motivation and teamwork [k], which matters when engineers will work alongside 85 production staff at the Dunwick plant [app], so relying on tests alone could appoint technically strong but difficult colleagues [an]. Overall, on balance the company should use tests and then interview, because the $1,800 cost (about $100 per candidate) is small against the price of a wrong technical hire, and tests give the objective base the interviews lack [eval]. Both methods together give the most reliable route to appointing the right 6 engineers within three weeks [eval].
    Keywords: aptitude tests, 18 candidates, engineering drawings, $1,800, one-to-one interviews, 320 applications, 85 production staff
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Aptitude tests produce objective, measurable scores; Interviews reveal motivation and teamwork | application_max_2: Checks ability to read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems across 18 candidates; Cuts the field from 320 applications to 6 hires | analysis_max_2: Reduces risk of costly mis-hire in a technical environment; Test-only approach may miss motivation and teamwork fit | evaluation_max_2: Weighs $1,800 cost ($100 per candidate) against cost of a wrong hire; Concludes a combined tests-then-interviews approach is best

--- STEM ---
Caldermere Hotel Group runs 4 hotels in Country X and employs 320 staff. Its events coordinator at the Seacrest Grand Hotel resigned last month, leaving a vacancy earning $42,000 a year. The group has two strong internal candidates: Priya Nair, a banquet supervisor with 6 years of service, and Daniel Reyes, a conference sales team leader with 4 years of service.

Alternatively, the HR director could advertise externally and attract experienced events professionals from outside the group, at an estimated recruitment cost of $9,500 including advertising and agency fees. External advertising would take around 4 weeks and could attract 30 or more applicants. The chief executive must decide whether to promote internally or recruit from outside; whichever route is chosen, the post must be filled before the peak wedding season in June.

--- QUESTIONS ---
  Qa [2 marks]
    Question: Define 'internal recruitment'.
    Answer: Internal recruitment is filling a vacancy by appointing someone who already works for the business, for example through promotion or transfer, rather than hiring from outside the organisation. [2]
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Filling a vacancy with an existing employee; Includes promotion or transfer from within the business

  Qb [4 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of recruiting the events coordinator internally.
    Answer: Advantage 1: Internal candidates are already known to the group, so managers have direct evidence of their performance and reliability [k], meaning Priya Nair or Daniel Reyes' work as banquet supervisor and conference sales team leader is proven rather than untested [app]. Advantage 2: Filling the vacancy internally is quicker and cheaper [k], avoiding the estimated $9,500 cost of advertising and agency fees and allowing the post to be filled before the June wedding season [app]. [4]
    Keywords: internal candidates, Priya Nair, Daniel Reyes, $9,500, June, 6 years of service
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Internal candidates are already known and tested in the business; Quicker and cheaper than external recruitment | application_max_2: Proven records of Priya Nair (6 years) and Daniel Reyes (4 years); Avoids $9,500 external recruitment cost before June wedding season

  Qc [6 marks]
    Question: Explain two advantages of recruiting the events coordinator externally.
    Answer: Advantage 1: External recruitment widens the applicant pool beyond the 4 hotels [k], allowing experienced events professionals from outside the group to apply [app], so the group can appoint a coordinator with broader events expertise [an]. Advantage 2: An external hire brings fresh ideas and avoids internal rivalries [k], which matters if Priya Nair and Daniel Reyes both applied and one is appointed over the other [app], helping the events team work smoothly in the run-up to the June wedding season [an]. [6]
    Keywords: externally, $9,500, 4 hotels, events coordinator, wedding season, 30 or more applicants
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Widens the pool of applicants beyond the business; Brings fresh ideas and avoids internal rivalries | application_max_2: Access to experienced events professionals outside the group; Prevents awkwardness if one internal candidate beats the other | analysis_max_2: Broader events expertise strengthens the hotel's offering; Smooth team dynamics in the peak wedding season

  Qd [8 marks]
    Question: Do you think Caldermere Hotel Group should recruit the events coordinator internally or externally? Justify your answer.
    Answer: Caldermere Hotel Group should prioritise internal recruitment because Priya Nair and Daniel Reyes are proven performers whose work is already known across the 4 hotels [k], so appointing either avoids the $9,500 cost of external advertising and agency fees [app]. Filling the post quickly from within also protects service during the June wedding season, when occupancy peaks [an]. However, internal recruitment means one strong candidate may feel passed over [k], risking lower morale or even resignation in a hotel employing 320 staff [app], whereas an external hire would add fresh expertise but at extra cost and with a 4-week advertising timeline that could delay the appointment until after the June peak [an]. Overall, on balance the group should promote internally, choosing the stronger candidate on merit, because the cost saving, speed and known track records outweigh the modest benefit of outside experience for a coordinator post [eval]. The unsuccessful internal candidate should receive feedback and a development plan to protect morale [eval].
    Keywords: internal candidates, Priya Nair, Daniel Reyes, $9,500, June, wedding season, 320 staff
    Mark scheme: knowledge_max_2: Internal candidates are proven and known to managers; External hires bring fresh experience at extra cost | application_max_2: Avoids $9,500 recruitment cost and delays before June; Ripple effect on morale across 320 staff and the wedding season | analysis_max_2: Faster appointment safeguards peak-season service; Risk of morale damage or delay if external route is chosen | evaluation_max_2: Balanced judgement favouring internal promotion on merit; Recognises need for feedback to retain the unsuccessful candidate
